Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

for context, we use PagePin in Chrome on the shared lab laptops and on our own computers. the extension saves the page title, address, capture time, and any note typed into the panel. it does not save the page itself, and i don't want this request to sound like a change to what information gets collected. the panel currently has a title field, a note box, a collection menu, and a blue Save button. after a save, the panel disappears and the small PagePin icon shows the saved count. that behavior is simple to understand, even if it interrupts a longer batch of captures.

last Tuesday, my colleague Theo tried a sequence of article captures while preparing the coastal-planning packet. he saved a city report, opened a second tab, and then opened the PagePin panel again to save a university brief. he repeated that cycle for seven pages. Theo did the test on his own laptop, not on a shared machine, and he was using the current public version of Chrome. he told me, “I keep reopening the same little panel, and it breaks my place in the reading.” that was his description of the task, not a claim that PagePin lost any of his notes. i watched him finish the packet, but i did not count how much time the repeated openings took.

Theo also tried pinning the panel from Chrome's toolbar. that kept the toolbar visible, but it did not keep PagePin's capture panel open after he pressed Save. he later switched back to the ordinary panel because the pinned view took space from the article. i haven't checked whether Chrome behaves the same way on every operating system, and i don't know if the extension can tell which panel layout a person is using. those details may matter to Luis when he looks at the request, so i want to keep them as questions rather than assume an answer.

my request to Luis is to consider a small preference called something like “Keep the capture panel open after saving.” i'm not attached to that exact label. the setting could be in PagePin's options page, near the existing choice for the default collection, rather than appearing as another control inside every capture. if Luis thinks the options page is not the right place, i'm open to a different location. the important part for me is that this is an individual preference and that the existing close-after-save behavior can still be selected.

there are a few details that might make the request easier to review:
1. the preference should let a person choose whether Save closes the panel or leaves it open for another capture; it should not change the saved title, address, capture time, or note.
2. when the panel remains open, the current page's saved information should not appear as if it were a new unsaved capture. the person would need to be able to move to another page and start a separate capture in the usual way.
3. the collection menu should continue to show the collection selected for the next save, rather than silently switching to a different collection. if PagePin already refreshes that menu as a person changes collections, this request isn't asking to alter that rule.
4. the preference should be easy to reverse, so a person who tries it can return to automatic closing without reinstalling the extension or losing their saved items.

these are the behaviors i have in mind, not a claim about how the extension is built today. i haven't inspected PagePin's code, and i don't know whether the panel can reset its fields after a save without closing. i would rather Luis decide whether that is practical than suggest a technical implementation that might not fit the extension. i can share the coastal-planning example with him if it helps, but i haven't sent him Theo's notes or asked Theo to file a separate issue.

there is also a condition that matters for how this could be used: if someone is working on a shared lab laptop, they should be able to leave the setting off and keep the current close-after-save behavior. i don't want a choice made on my own computer to change the experience for everyone who uses a lab laptop. i assume the preference would belong to the browser profile, but i haven't confirmed how PagePin stores its existing options, so that part needs checking rather than being treated as settled. Theo did his captures on his own laptop; he didn't change any preference on the shared machines.

Maya, our project coordinator, asked me to put the request in writing before the next planning meeting, and Luis is the person i am asking to review it. Maya did not ask Luis to build the setting, and i have not told the group that it will be included. i can send Luis the approximate date of Theo's test and the Chrome version if he needs them; i have not recorded the exact version number yet. the packet included a city transportation report, a university brief, two maps, and several policy pages, so the repeated capture flow came up while moving among different kinds of sources, not just near-identical web pages.

i'd also like to be clear about what would count as a useful discussion with Luis. he could tell me whether a per-profile preference is feasible, ask for details about the panel behavior, or suggest a different way to handle a run of captures. i'm asking him to consider the setting, not requesting that he promise a release date or say the feature is approved. if the panel cannot stay open without causing another problem, i would want to hear what constraint he found before we talk about alternatives. i can describe what Theo did, but i can't speak for how every member of the group would choose to use the preference.

for the next planning meeting, i'll bring the current PagePin screen description, Theo's account of reopening the panel seven times, and the condition about keeping shared laptop profiles independent from my own. the meeting is scheduled for Thursday afternoon in the small conference room, and Maya asked me to send Luis the written request beforehand so he has time to look at it. i have not yet sent it. the request should remain focused on the panel after saving, with the saved information and collection behavior staying as they are, unless Luis identifies a technical detail that needs a separate conversation.", "output": "I’m writing about a preference for PagePin, the browser extension our small research group uses to save articles and notes.
